findings.description: The script downloads real, licence-less production customer photographs to a persistent local path (`tempfile.gettempdir()` by default, which is not auto-cleaned on many systems) with no retention/cleanup guidance beyond "don't commit them". Given these are customer-submitted images, the safety contract should say what happens to them after inspection (e.g., required deletion, no re-upload, no inclusion in bug reports).
findings.suggestion: Extend the safety-contract docstring with an explicit retention/cleanup expectation for the downloaded files, or have the script offer to delete them after use.

findings.description: Unlike its sibling `prod-result-dimensions.py`, this script doesn't validate that `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` actually looks like a service-role key (dot count / `sb_secret_` prefix) nor reject a localhost/127.0.0.1 URL. The two scripts share almost identical preambles but diverge in safety checks for no stated reason.
findings.suggestion: Factor the shared validation (`die`, URL/key checks, `api()`) into a small common helper module so both scripts enforce the same guardrails.

findings.description: Same unpaginated PostgREST query as the dimensions script. If the jobs table exceeds PostgREST's default row cap, one of the target job ids could legitimately exist but fall outside the returned page, and the script would incorrectly report it as "NOT found in the jobs table".
findings.suggestion: Add explicit pagination (or an id-based filter, e.g. `id=in.(...)` built from the wanted prefixes) instead of fetching the whole table and filtering client-side.

findings.description: `dimensions()` calls `struct.unpack` on slices derived from only the first 2048 bytes of the object. For a JPEG whose SOF marker segment extends past the fetched range, or any truncated/malformed header, `struct.unpack` raises `struct.error`, which is not caught anywhere in the per-job loop (only `urllib.error.URLError` is caught). A single such object aborts the whole census instead of being logged as "unreadable".
findings.suggestion: Wrap the `dimensions(raw)` call (or the unpack calls themselves) in a try/except that falls through to the existing "header not recognised"/unreadable path.

findings.description: The jobs query has no `limit`/pagination handling and relies on PostgREST's default page size (commonly 1000 rows). If the `jobs` table has more rows than that, the scan silently covers only a subset, yet the script prints a confident verdict ("CONFIRMED: no production job has ever exercised Cloud AI at a real phone's resolution") based on the incomplete set. Since this script's whole purpose is to produce an authoritative count used to justify a technical decision, an undetected truncation would produce a false conclusion.
findings.suggestion: Either request `Prefer: count=exact` and compare against `len(jobs)`, or loop with `Range`/`offset` headers until all rows are retrieved, and print a warning if truncation is suspected.

note: telemetry incomplete (none); cost is the settled counter delta
